channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Presidente do PT cita 'cultura golpista' de Flávio e Jair Bolsonaro e diz que não se pode tolerar ataques ao processo eleitoral
item.description: PT president Edinho Silva accused Senator Flávio Bolsonaro of adopting a 'coup culture' similar to his father Jair Bolsonaro by spreading unfounded doubts about Brazil's electronic voting machines at an international event. Flávio claimed many voting machines used in Brazil are from a company tied to Venezuela's Smartmatic, linking them to alleged fraud in Venezuela and under U.S. investigation, despite the TSE repeatedly stating that Smartmatic does not supply voting machines or software for Brazilian elections.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro vem fazendo exatamente o que Lula e o PT espera dele
item.description: By repeating the false claim about Venezuelan-made electronic voting machines during a meeting with foreign ambassadors, Flávio Bolsonaro undermined his self-portrayal as a moderate and handed Lula and the PT exactly what they hoped for: a divisive figure who revives the specter of Bolsonarism. His candidacy has become an indirect tool of the PT’s strategy, weakening the right and shielding Lula from backlash over his government’s declining popularity.

item.title: Lula é rejeitado por 47% e Flávio, por 46%, diz pesquisa
item.description: Lula is rejected by 47% and Flávio Bolsonaro by 46%, according to a Gerp poll released on July 22, 2026. The survey, conducted among 2,000 respondents between July 15 and 17, has a 95% confidence level and is registered with the TSE under BR-05026/2026. The stimulated poll asked respondents which candidates they would never vote for.

item.title: Sem provas, Flávio Bolsonaro ataca sistema eleitoral com boatos antigos
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro repeated unfounded allegations against Brazil’s electoral system, claiming electronic voting machines were made by the Venezuelan company Smartmatic and linked to alleged fraud cited by the CIA, despite the Electoral Justice having debunked these claims for six years. His speech occurred exactly two years after his father Jair Bolsonaro’s similar address at the Alvorada Palace, which led to his ineligibility until 2030 and subsequent conviction for attempting a coup. Flávio’s actions represent a deliberate repetition of the Bolsonaro family’s strategy to delegitimize elections without presenting evidence.

item.title: Flávio e Lula têm empate técnico no 2º turno, diz pesquisa
item.description: A Gerp poll released on July 22, 2026 shows a technical tie between Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) and President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) in a hypothetical 2026 presidential runoff, with 46% and 45% voting intentions respectively, within a 2.19-point margin of error. The survey interviewed 2,000 people from July 15–17, with 95% confidence level and TSE registration BR-05026/2026. Both candidates exhibit high rejection rates: 47% for Lula and 46% for Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Uma má notícia para Paulo Pimenta
item.description: A Paraná Pesquisas poll shows petista Paulo Pimenta in fourth place in the Rio Grande do Sul Senate race with 23.7% voting intentions. As Lula's government leader in the Chamber of Deputies and former Secom minister, he trails behind other candidates, signaling a setback for his campaign.

item.title: Juliana Brizola é rejeitada por 27,3% dos eleitores no RS
item.description: Juliana Brizola (PDT) is the most rejected candidate in Rio Grande do Sul for the 2026 elections, with 27.3% of voters stating they would not vote for her, according to a Paraná Pesquisas survey conducted between July 16 and 19, 2026. Federal Deputy Luciano Zucco (PL) ranks second in rejection. The poll, with a margin of error of 2.6 percentage points and 95% confidence level, was funded by the Liberal Party and registered with the TSE under RS-09313/2026.

item.title: Um plano de governo para o eleitor do Bolsonaro raiz
item.description: Renan Santos of the Missão party unveiled a detailed government plan as a campaign differentiator, emphasizing fiscal reforms, deep changes to the federal pact, and a strict security policy — rare among Brazilian candidates often rely on generic slogans. The documentaing fiscal reforms, federal pact changes, and a strict security agenda — uncommon among Brazilian presidential candidates who typically rely on vague slogans. The proposal targets the core Bolsonaro electorate with concrete, structural measures. O Antagonista highlighted the move as a bold step in the 2026 electoral landscape.

item.title: Palmeiras encara o Coritiba sem Flaco López e Vitor Roque; veja odds
item.description: Palmeiras faces Coritiba away in the 19th round of the Brasileirão without strikers Flaco López and Vitor Roque, who are unavailable due to international duty and post-surgery recovery. Abel Ferreira relies on Ramón Sosa and Jhon Arias to score, as the Verdão leads the league with 41 points and remains favored despite playing away. Odds show 1.85 for a Palmeiras win, 3.40 for a draw, and 4.33 for Coritiba.

item.title: Agenda de Lula: leia os compromissos do presidente nesta 4ª feira
item.description: President Lula spends the day at the Palácio do Planalto focused on economic agenda, including a meeting with the Civil House, a meeting with Stellantis global and regional executives to discuss the automotive sector, and the signing of Bill of Conversion No. 7/2026, which allocates resources to the Brasil Soberano credit program. The agenda includes the presence of Vice President Geraldo Alckmin and government ministers.

item.title: Governo Lula: leia a agenda de ministros nesta 4ª feira
item.description: On Wednesday (July 22, 2026), the Lula government's agenda focuses on the automotive sector, international diplomacy, and culture. Ministers from the Civil House, Development, and Finance are meeting with Stellantis executives at the Planalto Palace, while Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira attends the 3rd Brazil-ASEAN Trilateral Meeting in Manila, and Culture Minister Margareth Menezes attends the Flip literary festival in Paraty. Out of 38 ministers, only 6 had their schedules disclosed.

item.title: Saiba quais são as pesquisas que saem nesta 4ª feira
item.description: New electoral studies registered with the TSE are cleared for publication starting Wednesday, July 22, 2026, covering national surveys and voting intentions in seven Brazilian states: Espírito Santo, Maranhão, Mato Grosso do Sul, Paraná, Piauí, Rio Grande do Norte, and Rio Grande do Sul. The polls may only be released after meeting the legal minimum waiting period and upon registration with the Electoral Justice. Poder360 offers a Poll Aggregator for Drive subscribers, providing access to thousands of surveys since 2000.

item.title: PSB deve sugerir tarifa zero no transporte público para plano de governo de Lula
item.description: The PSB, the party of Vice President Geraldo Alckmin, is expected to propose the inclusion of free public transportation in major cities within Lula’s government plan for a potential fourth term. The suggestion comes from the João Mangabeira Foundation, the PSB’s political training arm, which is participating in discussions over the PT’s program. The measure aims to expand urban transit access and reduce costs for the population.

item.title: E Dudu, hein?
item.description: A survey of 300 readers shows that 53.3% believe Eduardo Bolsonaro should stay in the United States permanently, while 41.7% think he should return to Brazil to be arrested. Only 5% suggest he should do what's best for his father, Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: Para 51%, governo Lula é melhor que o de Bolsonaro, diz PoderData
item.description: 51% of Brazilians consider President Lula's government better than Bolsonaro's, according to a PoderData survey from July 2026, showing a 10-point increase over two months. The share viewing Lula's administration as worse dropped to 34%, with 8% seeing them as equal and 6% undecided. The Northeast shows the highest approval (63%), and among low-income earners (up to 2 minimum wages), 56% view the petista government as better.

item.title: PoderData: após tarifaço, aprovação pessoal de Lula vai a 46%
item.description: Following the tariff increase, President Lula's personal approval rose to 46%, tying with 47% disapproval, according to PoderData's July 2026 survey. Government approval also improved slightly to 43% (from 42%), while disapproval remained stable at 51%, signaling a break from months of negative trends. The poll surveyed 2,500 respondents nationwide via landline and mobile calls, with a 2-point margin of error at 95% confidence.

item.title: Tarifaço de Trump joga água no chope da convenção de Flávio
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro faced an unexpected setback just days before the convention that would formalize his 2026 presidential candidacy, following Donald Trump’s announcement of new trade tariffs that triggered economic instability and undermined his campaign’s optimistic outlook. The tariff measures disrupted the favorable economic conditions he had hoped to secure by mid-semester, creating pressure on his narrative of growth and stability. What was meant to be a triumphant convention now unfolds under a cloud of economic uncertainty and doubts about his ability to manage external shocks.

item.title: Tarifaço repercute de forma diferente no Instagram, X e WhatsApp
item.description: The 25% additional tariff imposed by the United States on part of Brazilian exports took effect today, triggering varied reactions across social media: on Instagram, visual content highlights affected producers; on X, the debate is more polarized with accusations of protectionism; on WhatsApp, alarmist messages circulated about job impacts and consumer costs.

item.title: Onde Lula e Flávio enfrentam maiores problemas nos palanques estaduais
item.description: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro are struggling to form alliances in key states such as Rio de Janeiro and Minas Gerais, where local parties resist unified slates. Party conventions reveal weaknesses in national coordination, with disagreements over majoritarian candidacies and disputes over ticket placements.

item.title: Tarcísio avalia não ir à convenção do PSD após Kassab publicar montagem do governador com Caiado
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas is considering not attending the PSD convention in person after a post by Gilberto Kassab associated him with Ronaldo Caiado, a rival of his supported candidate Flávio Bolsonaro. The move aims to avoid being photographed alongside Caiado, which could generate campaign material for the Goiás candidate and mislead voters about an alleged alignment. Tarcísio may participate remotely or via a pre-recorded video, maintaining only the state-level PSD endorsement for his re-election.

item.title: Novo tarifaço de Trump contra o Brasil começa nesta quarta-feira
item.description: The U.S. imposed a 25% additional tariff on Brazilian goods, affecting around 2,400 companies and $7.4 billion in exports, with sectors like wood, machinery, furniture, ceramics, footwear, and sugar most impacted. The Brazilian government views the move as having a strong political component, tied to pressure on Bolsonaro and the STF, but has chosen not to retaliate, instead pursuing negotiations and cautious use of the Reciprocity Law.

item.title: Eleição: segurança de presidenciáveis impacta calendário de convenções
item.description: The Federal Police began deploying security teams for 2026 presidential pre-candidates as party conventions started between July 20 and August 5. Romeu Zema (Novo), Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), and Renan Santos (Missão) will request formal state protection, with Renan advancing his convention due to threats from PCC and CV. The operation is estimated to cost R$ 95 million, using armored vehicles, anti-drone systems, and up to 458 trained agents, while Lula will be protected by the GSI.

item.title: Tal pai (Jair Bolsonaro), tal filho (Flávio), ambos golpistas
item.description: The article criticizes Jair and Flávio Bolsonaro for spreading disinformation about Brazil's electronic voting machines, falsely linking the system to Venezuelan fraud and calling for international observers, despite the TSE confirming that Smartmatic did not supply voting machines or software in Brazil. The narrative seeks to undermine trust in the electoral process, repeating patterns of attacks on the judiciary and voting system, with the goal of questioning the legitimacy of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro ganhou green card igual ao de Paulo Figueiredo
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro received a U.S. green card in July under the 'extraordinary abilities' category, similar to journalist Paulo Figueiredo, who obtained his in 2023. The card also extends to his wife and two children, granting permanent residency, as Eduardo has been living in self-exile in the U.S. since February 2025 due to legal proceedings in Brazil’s STF. Despite the benefit, he stated he will not pursue U.S. citizenship and intends to return to Brazil after five years.

item.title: Tarifaço: governo estuda socorro aos setores nos moldes de 2025
item.description: The Lula government plans to extend the Brazil Sovereign Plan to aid exporters hit by new 25% U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods, effective July 22. Building on last year’s experience, the measure will use extraordinary credit via BNDES/FGE, albeit at a reduced scale due to tariff exemptions. Productive sector meetings have already taken place to tailor relief and identify U.S. companies that may be adversely affected.

item.title: Por que novo tarifaço de Trump não deve decidir eleição a favor de Lula
item.description: Trump's new tariff hike is unlikely to decide the 2026 election in favor of Lula, as swing voters prioritize national sovereignty only after negotiation, not submission. Lula’s government improved its approval in 2025 by championing sovereignty following the first tariff, but the current context is more complex and hinges on how negotiations are perceived. Research with undecided voters shows sovereignty is valued only when it follows dialogue, not unilateral imposition.

item.title: Lula amplia núcleo de campanha após atritos entre equipe
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) expanded the core of his re-election campaign, reassigning members of the so-called "kitchen" of the Palácio do Planalto to the team coordinated by PT president Edinho Silva. The move aims to overcome internal frictions and strengthen political coordination ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Aliados de Derrite se queixam de falta de empenho de Tarcísio e prioridade a André do Prado
item.description: Allies of the São Paulo PP complain that Governor Tarcísio de Freitas is not adequately supporting Guilherme Derrite, the party's Senate nominee, despite Derrite having served as his former public security secretary. Derrite ranks fifth in the Datafolha poll, and PP members believe Tarcísio is prioritizing André do Prado over his former ally.

item.title: Renan Santos: o outsider candidato à Presidência - O Assunto #1766
item.description: Renan Santos, founder of the MBL, was officially nominated as the presidential candidate for the Missão party, formed in 2025 from the movement. His government plan proposes 'favelization eradication', war on organized crime, municipal mergers, and ending Bolsa Família, inspired by Javier Milei and Nayib Bukele. The candidacy positions him as an anti-Lula and anti-Flávio Bolsonaro outsider in the 2026 political landscape.

item.title: Aliados apontam razões que podem fazer Cleitinho recuar de candidatura
item.description: Cleitinho Azevedo (Republicanos) remains undecided about running for governor of Minas Gerais, despite polling around 30% in voter intentions and support from allies like Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). While allies highlight his strong grassroots appeal in the state’s interior, they cite personal concerns and political controversies — including alleged ties to a land conflict killing in Amazonas involving his Senate alternate and corruption allegations against Republicanos state leader Euclydes Pettersen — as factors that may lead him to withdraw.

item.title: Redes de la nueva derecha entre Europa y América Latina
item.description: The victory of far-right candidates in countries like Colombia and Argentina, combined with Trump's influence on Latin American elections and the presidential race in Brazil between Lula and Bolsonaro, suggests a deeper ideological shift beyond mere protest voting. The article argues that understanding the structure, ideology, and organization of these new right-wing forces is essential for progressives to develop effective counter-strategies.

item.title: Soberania nacional não se improvisa
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated he does not want war nor to be caught off guard, emphasizing the importance of national preparedness. His remark raises the enduring question of why states invest in military capabilities that may never be used, a core dilemma in the formation of modern states.

item.title: A três dias de lançar candidatura, Flávio Bolsonaro está atrasado
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro is lagging in his campaign preparations, with just three days left before the official launch of his candidacy. He has not yet selected a running mate and remains uncertain about which parties will support him. This situation raises doubts about the structure and viability of his electoral campaign.

item.title: De Lisboa a Pyongyang: onde estão os brasileiros aptos a votar no exterior
item.description: The Brazilian electorate abroad grew 31.8% since 2022, reaching 918,9 thousand voters, driven mainly by immigration to Portugal and the United States. Lisbon led the growth with a 74.1% increase, reaching 78.8 thousand voters, while the U.S. remains the country with the highest number of registered Brazilian voters (265.4 thousand). The top ten voting locations concentrate 46.2% of the overseas electorate, reflecting high concentration in a few key destinations.

item.title: Tarifaço de 25% sobre produtos brasileiros entra em vigor hoje nos EUA: entenda o que muda para os exportadores
item.description: The United States has imposed a 25% additional tariff on part of Brazilian exports, affecting sectors such as wood, furniture, machinery, footwear, ceramics, and sugar, with an estimated impact of $5.8 billion. Despite the measure, key products like oil, beef, aircraft, pulp, and coffee were excluded, and the Lula government is negotiating to mitigate the effects, including a possible additional 12.5% tariff linked to forced labor allegations.

item.title: Tarifaço: por que o Brasil evita uma retaliação imediata — e como pode responder aos EUA
item.description: The Lula government chose not to immediately retaliate against the U.S. 25% tariff on certain Brazilian exports, aiming to avoid giving political ammunition to Trump and Flávio Bolsonaro ahead of elections. Instead, it is pursuing diplomatic negotiations and expanding exemption lists, while keeping the Economic Reciprocity Law as a future option.

item.title: Brasil opta por la cautela para responder a los nuevos aranceles impuestos por Estados Unidos
item.description: Brazil has adopted a cautious stance in response to the new 25% U.S. tariffs on Brazilian imports, despite initially threatening retaliation under its reciprocity law. Vice President Geraldo Alckmin warned that symmetrical retaliation would lead to mutual harm, citing the metaphor 'an eye for an eye and we will end up blind'. So far, Brasília has not activated concrete retaliatory measures.

item.title: Vereadora do PT diz que Tarcísio promove “desmonte” em SP
item.description: São Paulo city councilwoman Luna Zarattini (PT-SP) accused Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) of promoting a "dismantling" of public education in the state, citing deteriorating school infrastructure, teacher burnout due to digital platform policies, and failures in sanitation and transport. She also criticized the privatization of Sabesp and concessions in metropolitan trains and subways, attacked the Bolsonaro family over the Master case, and endorsed Fernando Haddad as a strong candidate to defeat Bolsonarism in São Paulo.

item.title: Pesquisa BTG/Nexus mostra disputa Lula x Flávio após tarifaço dos EUA
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll, to be released on July 27, will assess the impact of the U.S. tariffs on Brazil on voter intentions for the 2026 presidential election. The survey will measure the contest between Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), along with other candidates, and analyze how the trade crisis influences voter perceptions of the two main contenders, including whom they believe is right in the dispute.

item.title: Republicanos perde ação contra boneco de urna eletrônica e Parada LGBT
item.description: The São Paulo Regional Electoral Court (TRE-SP) dismissed a lawsuit filed by the Republicans party against APOLGBT-SP and the Instituto Plena Cidadania for alleged premature electoral propaganda, ruling that banners and the inflatable 'Votinho' urn with slogans like 'Vote LGBT 2026' and 'The Street Calls, the Ballot Confirms' constitute generic calls for political participation, not targeted endorsements. The judge emphasized the absence of an explicit vote request, which is necessary to characterize premature electoral propaganda. The 30th São Paulo LGBT+ Pride Parade took place without the attendance of Governor Tarcísio de Freitas or Mayor Ricardo Nunes.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro rebate Caiado e direita fica mais rachada
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro countered Ronaldo Caiado's criticism of his U.S. green card, accusing the former governor of staying silent on January 8 convictions and using Goiás citizenship to favor STF allies. The exchange, including Caiado's Disney-themed poll as an indirect jab, deepens divisions on the Brazilian right and undermines prospects for a Caiado-Flávio Bolsonaro alliance in a potential 2026 runoff.

item.title: Tereza Cristina rejeita, Daniella Marques traz dificuldade. O que sobra para vice de Flávio? O desespero
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro has yet to finalize his vice-presidential pick for the 2026 elections, despite the PL convention scheduled for March 25. Senator Tereza Cristina has been ruled out as an option, while economist Daniella Marques of the Republicans remains the favorite, contingent on a PL-Republicans coalition that has not yet materialized. The campaign is struggling to close the ticket, with the vice-presidential decision potentially delayed until the following weeks, within the legal timeframe.

item.title: Em evento com diplomatas, Flávio questiona segurança das urnas
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro questioned the security of Brazil's electronic voting machines at a diplomatic event, citing CIA reports on Venezuela and claiming that Smartmatic machines used in Venezuela are also used in Brazil. The TSE denied the claims, stating Smartmatic has never supplied or accessed Brazilian voting machines or software, only providing technical training in 2020 and losing a bid to Positivo. Flávio clarified he does not question the voting process itself and urged more international observers to enhance election transparency.

item.title: Caiado rebate Eduardo Bolsonaro citando personagens da Disney: ‘Pateta da política brasileira’
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado provoked Eduardo Bolsonaro on social media by comparing him to the 'Goofy of Brazilian politics', suggesting his actions in the U.S. harm Brazil's economy. The exchange followed the revelation of a green card granted by Donald Trump to Eduardo Bolsonaro and his family, which sparked mutual criticism. Caiado accused Eduardo of damaging Brazil-U.S. relations, while Eduardo countered by accusing Caiado of staying silent on those convicted in the January 8 coup attempt and seeking favor with Brasilia's elite and the STF.

item.title: A disparada de Renan, o alerta para Zema e outras movimentações na pesquisa Real Time Big Data
item.description: The Real Time Big Data poll shows Renan Santos at 9% in first-round voting intentions, ahead of Ronaldo Caiado (7%), highlighting his growth as an alternative to Lula-Bolsonaro polarization. While Renan rises, Romeu Zema loses traction on the right, with voters shifting to Caiado and Renan. Flávio Bolsonaro recovers in the runoff scenario, tying technically with Lula (42% to 45%) after a prior streak of declining polls.

item.title: Após citar dado falso sobre urna a diplomatas, Flávio diz que 'não coloca em dúvida o processo eleitoral brasileiro'
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro denied having questioned the Brazilian electoral process after citing false information about the origin of electronic voting machines at an event with foreign diplomats. He stated that inviting international observers strengthens transparency, despite having referenced discredited claims about the Venezuelan company Smartmatic, which the TSE has refuted. The remarks were made during the 'Debating Brazil' event attended by diplomats from 42 countries.

item.title: Debates em 2026: Lula vai encarar ou fugir? #brasil #debate #política
item.description: The content discusses the potential for presidential debates in 2026, focusing on the expectation of whether President Lula will participate or avoid direct confrontations with his opponents. No specific candidates or detailed policy proposals are mentioned — only a rhetorical question about his stance in debate events. The tone is speculative and aimed at driving social media engagement.

item.title: Coordenador da campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro diz que Michelle segue candidata
item.description: The coordinator of Flávio Bolsonaro's pre-campaign, Senator Rogério Marinho, stated that the PL party continues to support Michelle Bolsonaro as its Senate pre-candidate for the Federal District, despite her recent absence following claims of mistreatment by her stepson. The statement aims to stabilize her candidacy amid speculation about her potential withdrawal from the race.

item.title: Amiga de Lulinha pede apuração sobre vazamento de conversa
item.description: The defense of businesswoman Roberta Luchsinger has requested the Federal Supreme Court to investigate a possible leak of private conversations with Lulinha, son of former President Lula, intended for use in Flávio Bolsonaro’s pre-campaign. The request follows an O Globo report indicating that Bolsonaro’s campaign planned to release audio related to the INSS fraud investigation. The defense claims no judicial authorization was granted for the interception and seeks access to the materials or an investigation into illegal breach of privacy.

item.title: Cacique ‘sincerão’: relembre seis declarações polêmicas de Valdemar Costa Neto, presidente do PL
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto, president of the PL, reiterated controversial statements by claiming Flávio Bolsonaro was unprepared for a presidential run and needed Michelle Bolsonaro, Tarcísio de Freitas, and Nikolas Ferreira on the front lines to win. He also defended the practice of party leaders directing parliamentary amendments without holding elected office, prompting criticism and a formal inquiry from Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino. These remarks underscore his reputation for blunt speech and are causing friction within and beyond the Bolsonarist base.
